fields.label: Intro sentence
paragraphs: A moulded rubber packing pad, open on one side, so it slides in beside a bolt or shaft instead of over it. It carries load and holds a gap — and because it is slotted, it can be fitted or replaced in service without dismantling the assembly around it.

fields.label: Wrong default, and a missing option
paragraphs: 🛑 Natural rubber is not on the menu, and it has the best fatigue resistance and highest resilience of the eight Margo mixes — which is what a pad that is loaded and unloaded for years is judged on.

🛑 EPDM is pre-selected. It weathers well and creeps more than natural rubber under sustained load, and on a pad whose job is to hold a gap, creep is the failure. The default should follow the duty rather than the weather.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked, and the four missing from the live selector are added.

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: Goes on without taking anything apart

The slot lets the pad slide in beside a bolt or shaft rather than over it. On a service job that is the difference between slackening a fastener and stripping an assembly — which is usually why the shape was chosen in the first place.
Hardness will not tell you how it behaves

Rubber bulges rather than compresses, so a thin wide pad is far stiffer than a thick narrow one of the same compound. Send the load and the gap you need held, and we set the shape and the hardness together.
It keeps sinking after you fit it
Rubber under permanent load creeps for years, and a packing pad that loses 2 mm has stopped doing its job. We allow for it at the design stage rather than shipping a pad that is correct on day one.
🛑 Tell us what holds it in

An open pad has one less thing keeping it in place than a closed one. Friction, a groove, adhesive or captive under the fastener — the answer changes the hardness and sometimes the outline, and it is the question that prevents a pad walking out under vibration.

sections.title: Global applications
sections.live: LIVE H2 → Global Applications · Aerospace and Marine claimed here and on all 31 pages

fields.label: Why industries are the right frame here
paragraphs: A slotted packing pad is not tied to one vehicle or one machine. It is a generic serviceability part — wherever a gap has to be held beside a fastener and the assembly should not have to come apart to change it. So the industry grid is the correct frame; it needs industries where that situation actually arises.
leads: A slotted packing pad is not tied to one vehicle or one machine.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: The slot changes tooling and inspection
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · the same text as all 31 pages

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The compound is chosen for creep resistance first, since the pad has to hold a gap for years.

Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. Outline and thickness are set together to reach the load and deflection, and the slot root is radiused rather than square, because a sharp corner is where a slotted pad tears.
Post-cure and trimming, with the slot edges finished so nothing is left to initiate a tear.
Quality inspection — slot width gauged against the fastener size, plus dimensional check, hardness and load-deflection on batch samples.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Pads are packed flat and unloaded, since rubber stored under compression takes a set. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept. The live text says “ISO-certified lab” in step 01, which becomes “in-house lab”; step 04 is “Post-Cure & Trimming” and gains the slot-edge detail.
🛑 The radiused slot root in step 02 is the engineering point of the whole sheet. A slot is a stress raiser, tearing starts at its corner, and a square root will fail long before the rubber is worn out. Naming it as a tooling decision is what shows Margo has made slotted parts before.
Step 05 gauges the slot against the fastener, which is the check that stops a batch arriving that will not fit

notes: The process block must render from the part record.
“Radiused slot root” and “slot width gauged against the fastener” are the credibility markers on this page.
Numbered steps are an <ol>.

sections.title: Certified to international standards
sections.chip: EN 1337 is the misreading to close off
sections.live: LIVE H2 → Certified to International Standards · ISO 9001 only — honest

fields.label: Credit, an addition, a caution
paragraphs: ISO 9001:2015 claimed and nothing else — no IATF, no TÜV SÜD, no CE marking. The production table prints “On request” rather than inventing figures, and the video says “Film pending”. The scope covers a moulded pad, so the badge stands unqualified.

🛑 The risk on any load-bearing pad is structural bearings. A rubber packing pad is visually indistinguishable from an elastomeric bridge or building bearing, and those are certified products under EN 1337 with CE marking and third-party surveillance. Margo holds none of it, and an unqualified “certified to international standards” heading beside a load pad invites exactly that enquiry.
Add the client-instructed IATF line (2026-08-31): upgrading to IATF 16949, targeted end 2026; ISO 14001 and 45001 targeted 2027 — stated as a plan, never as held.
